In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a sensitive immunochemical technique for the detection of platinum adducts in DNA.
the application of the immunochemical detection method to the study of the quantitative distribution of the different Pt-DNA adducts in CHO cells treated with cis-platin.
the development and application of immunoassays for the quantitative determination of specific Pt-DNA-lesions in mammalian cells treated with cis-platin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intrastrand cross-links are responsible for the cytotoxic effect and the monofunctional lesions for the cytostatic activity.
cis-Pt(NHNH2)2d(pGG) is the most prominent lesion and the one that most probably is responsible for the cytotoxicity and mutagenicity of cisplatin.

, in CHO cells treated with cis-Pt(Nh3)2Cl2, the major DNA lesions are intrastrand cross-links between two guanines, with a smaller fraction of interstrand cross-linking between guanines and monofunctional binding of platinum to guanine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cisplatin forms intrastrand cross-links and interstrand cross-links in DNA, but that the interstrand cross-links are removed very rapidly after treatment of the cells, whereas the intrastrand cross-links are more stable.

, after a 2-h treatment with 83 micromolar cisplatin, cis-Pt2d(pG-pG) was formed in CHO cells at a level of 35.9%, and after a 24-h incubation period, 46.4% of the total platinum was present as intrastrand cross-links.
the major lesions are cis-Pt(Nh3)2d (pGpG) and cis-Pt(NHi3)2dGMP (monofunctional adduction).
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with the immunochemical techniques, it is possible to quantify the various Pt-adducts in DNA after treatment of mammalian cells with cisplatin.
the immunochemical method is a useful tool to study the formation and removal of Pt-adducts in the DNA of living cells.
immunochemical methods can be used for quantitative analysis of DNA-adducts, provided the antibodies have a high affinity and specificity for the adduct of interest.
